pageCache.pageTitle: Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page – Our school is rooted in respect, kindness and resilience.
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Stone with Woodford CoE Primary School
Welcome from the Headteacher, Mr Hall.
It is with great joy and pride that I welcome you to Stone with Woodford C of E Primary School, where we are dedicated to helping our students “Let Their Light Shine” (Matthew 5:16) . Whether you are a prospective parent, a current member of our community, or simply curious about who we are, I hope this website gives you a clear sense of our vision, values and the vibrant life of our school.
We believe every child is a unique gift from God and our school is a place where kindness, respect and resilience are nurtured and flourish. We strive to create a safe and inspiring environment where children feel loved, challenged and empowered to become the best version of themselves.
Our school, founded in 1895 and located in Gloucestershire, is a voluntary controlled, small Church of England school that combines a warm and friendly atmosphere with high standards of educational achievement. We are proud to be part of the Severn Federation Academy Trust, a family of creative schools, learning together in inclusive, inspiring and nurturing communities where all children and adults are loved and achieve their best.
At Stone with Woodford, we believe in putting enjoyment at the heart of every child’s education within a Christian context, and strive to create a welcoming, inclusive community where every student is valued and respected.
Our facilities include four classrooms (which allows for plenty of space for our three classes to spread out when needed), a hall, two offices, a library, and additional rooms in our redeveloped cottage. We make excellent use of the space we have and are well-equipped to support the growth and development of our students, giving them every opportunity to flourish and thrive both as learners and as members of society.
Thank you for considering our school for your child’s education, and we hope to see you soon!

pageCache.text:
Vision and Values at Stone with Woodford Primary School
Stone with Woodford Primary School is a Church of England school, central to its community, that is committed to providing all of its children with a high-quality education. We believe that every child has the potential to succeed, and we are dedicated to helping them reach their full potential.
Our values are at the heart of everything we do. We believe in:
We believe that these values are essential for success in life. We teach our students to be respectful, kind, and resilient. We believe that these values will help them to become successful adults who contribute to their community.
Our vision is to be a school where all students can thrive. We want our students to be happy, healthy, and well-rounded. We want them to be prepared for the next phase of their schooling and beyond. We want them to be successful in education, career, and life.
We believe that our values and vision are in line with the teachings of Jesus Christ. In Matthew 5:16, Jesus says, “Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.” We believe that when we live our values, we are shining the light of Christ in the world. We are showing others what it means to be respectful, kind, and resilient. We are making a difference in the world. We are contributing positively ourselves to a wider community.
We are committed to providing our students with a high-quality education that will prepare them for success in life. We believe that our values and vision will help us to achieve our goals. We are excited to see what the each and every day holds for everyone at Stone with Woodford Primary School.
How We Live Our Values
We live our values in everything we do at Stone with Woodford Primary School. Here are a few examples:
We believe that our values are essential for success in life. We believe that these values will help them to become successful adults who contribute to their community.

pageCache.pageTitle: About us – Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page
pageCache.text:
Stone with Woodford Primary School is a voluntary controlled, small Church of England village school in Gloucestershire. In August 2013 we became an academy. The school combines a warm and friendly atmosphere with high standards of educational achievement, and puts enjoyment at the heart of every child’s education within a Christian context. In September 2026, we joined the Severn Federation Academy Trust, a move which will provide the school with wonderful support and more opportunities for us all to shine brightly before others.
Our school is one big family where everyone is valued and respected.
We are dedicated to: Let Your Light Shine (Matthew 5:16) through our values of respect, kindness and resilience.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Church – Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page
pageCache.text:
We are proudly linked with All Saints Church in Stone…
Our church school is supported very positively by All Saints Church which is a very short single footpath walk from the school gate. The children attend church at least once a week and many more opportunities are created throughout the year to foster this link.
At our school, we prioritise letting each child’s light shine (Matthew 5:16). We focus on different values each term. We take pride in recording our students’ thoughtful responses in our worship book.

Local Academy Committee – Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page
pageCache.text:
Our committee members are a critical part of our strong team. They provide strategic support and challenge to ensure that we are achieving the highest of aspirations.
Should you wish to get in touch with any of them, please contact our chair via email: chair@stone-with-woodford.gloucs.sch.uk
If you wish to view any of our publicly available documents regarding governance please visit the school or contact our Clerk at clerk@stone-with-woodford.gloucs.sch.uk.
The Role of the Local Academy Committee
The Local Academy Committee (LAC) includes representatives of the staff, parents, the community and the Diocese.
Our role as a committee is to set ambitious aims and objectives for the school. Working in close partnership with the Head Teacher and other staff, we aim to provide support and encouragement as well as recognising the school’s achievements. But we are also there to challenge and question the school to ensure that areas for improvement continue to be identified and pursued.
The committee meets regularly to discuss and make decisions regarding the management and direction of the school.
Being a committee member is a challenging but rewarding experience, and those volunteering are offered training to help them make a valuable contribution to the school’s development. Members also spend time in school on a regular basis and report on different aspects of the school.
The Head Teacher is a committee member and is responsible for the day to day running of the school in line with the school’s policies.
Foundation committee membersare appointed by the church to help ensure the Christian ethos is preserved and developed, and that RE and collective worship reflect the spirit of the Trust Deed.
Parent committee members are elected by the parent body, staff governors by the staff and the local community is also represented by community members. Most local committee members serve a four-year term.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND – Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
SENDCo – Mrs Louise Stancombe
Please contact the school office for all SEND enquiries – admin@stone-with-woodford.gloucs.sch.uk
They will direct your enquiry to Mrs Stancombe.
At Stone with Woodford C of E Primary School, we believe that every child should be nurtured in an environment that enables them to succeed and shine their light brightly. Every child is entitled to quality first teaching alongside exposure to a wide range of enriching experiences. To allow all children to achieve this, we will provide the necessary support to meet every individual need.
SEND Local Offer – Gloucestershire
The Children and Families Act (2014) introduced many changes to support for young people in Education with Special Educational Needs Disabilities (SEND). In England, Statements of Special Educational Needs and Learning Difficulty Assessments have now been replaced by Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plans. In Gloucestershire, there is a graduated pathway to support all children with additional needs. If you have any concerns about your child’s development, talk to the school in the first instance. Your child’s SENDCO will be able to help with any questions you may have.
SEND Information Report
SEND or Special Educational Needs and Disability is when pupils need additional or different provision to enable them to achieve their potential. It is when one or more of the following is a barrier to their learning:
• Language and Communication (C+I)
• Social, Mental and Emotional Health (SEMH)
• Cognition & Learning (C+L)
• Medical, Physical or Sensory Needs
At Stone with Woodford C of E the progress and attainment of all pupils is reviewed every term by the Senior Leadership Team and teaching staff, at which time provision may be adjusted to meet identified needs. If a child continues to have difficulty after intervention or has a high level of difficulty when they join us, they may be considered to have special educational need (SEND) and be placed on the SEND register. If you, as a parent have concerns, you should firstly speak to your child’s teacher and afterwards, may wish to contact the SENDCo. All relevant parties, including parents and child, are consulted as part of the school’s decision to place on the register. We value the dialogue between staff and parents and implement regular formal and informal meetings where all parties may raise concerns.
If your child goes onto the SEND register, a My Plan will be created by their class teacher. This document will include targets for your child, as well as information as to how all adults, including parents, can help them to achieve them. Each child has their own file which contains their My Plan and any resources which may be helpful to them in class. The My Plan is reviewed a minimum of 3 times a year in consultation with children, parents and the class teacher. The SENDCo will attend review meeting when asked to do so by parents or teachers. If you would like the SENDCo to attend parents evening, please let the class teacher know.
If multiple agencies are involved in providing support/guidance to help your child, a My Plan+ may be written. This would be carried out by the SENDCo with parents, the child and class teacher contributing.
If your child does not make progress after receiving such graduated support, we will discuss with you the possibility of putting your child forward for an Educational Health Care Plan (EHCP). An outcome of this process may be that objectives will be set for your child and some additional funding may be available to support his/her learning in school. School will support you through this process but we will also advise you of other independent agencies who can also provide additional support to you.
What does SEND support look like at Stone with Woodford?
The most important level of support for your child is first quality teaching but should they need additional provision, the SENDCo will work closely with the class teacher to plan and oversee this. Additional provision may include small group or 1:1 teaching, additional or different resources or strategies used to support their learning. We have TAs and teachers trained to deliver various intervention programs. These include:
The school employs a person to fill the role of pastoral TA. This is someone who is there to listen to your child and try to work through any worries they may have. The school also employs a mindfulness coach, using PE & Sport Premium funding alongside Pupil Premium funding, to support children in developing their regulation strategies and understanding their bodies.
The school employs a part-time SENDCo (Special Educational Needs and Disability Coordinator). The school ensures that any newly appointed SENCO meets the statutory qualification requirements set out in the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations and completes the mandatory NPQ for SENCOs within the required timescale.
All teaching staff are kept up to date with best practice to support pupils with SEND and in house training or courses to enhance expertise are arranged according to the needs of our pupils.
If your child has an Education Health Plan (EHCP) with funding attached, the provision provided would be discussed and planned for in meetings with parents and possibly other outside agencies (see next section for details). The funding may be spent on TA support for the child in school or in other ways to meet the needs of the ‘whole’ child.
Should your child struggle with, for example, reading, if appropriate staff in school may apply for additional time for the child to access the Year 6 SATs. They may also complete tests on a 1:1 basis. Each child’s needs would be assessed and appropriate support provided, following national guidance.
The main school building is a very old building and so changes to the site are limited. There are steps to the main building. There is no ramp in place. There are less steps to the rear of the main building. Wagtail Class, which houses the YR/Y1 classroom has a small step in. The cottage building is accessible without steps.
What if more is needed to support my child?
When a child needs additional provision that we are unable to provide through the school’s resources, we may consider putting your child forward to work with outside agencies or may contact them for advice. This could involve working with Educational Psychology Services or Advisory Teaching Teams as well as other outside agencies. This would only occur with parental permission and notes from work carried out would be shared with you. These agencies may include:
Should your child have a specific learning difficulty their provision will be looked at and planned for on an individual basis. If your child has one of the following learning difficulties, their provision may include some of the following:
Should your child have difficulty in meeting behaviour expectations we may look at structures in place and the physical space of the classroom. Additionally, social stories to support your child with any changes or school trips may be written.
Should any child need medical or personal care this is treated with sensitivity by all staff involved, ensuring the dignity and of the child is maintained. In consultation with parents, staff are trained by relevant professionals to undertake necessary tasks, following the child’s care plan. Children with medical or personal care needs are likely to need additional support when on school trips and/or residential trips. This would be planned for carefully and full risk assessment written along with the staff: ratio being modified if needed.
When a child on the SEND register transfers to our school or joins us from an Early Years Setting, discussions with the former setting are held and records are received and read. As the parent/carer, your child’s class teacher will discuss targets and concerns with you and similarly, do contact the school if you wish to discuss any concerns. If your child is transferring to another school, all records will be delivered to the receiving school and a meeting or discussion with the receiving school will be arranged. Should the child be transferring to a secondary school and have an EHC plan, a transfer review is held during year 5 where parents/carers and children may meet staff from the receiving school and the needs of the child are discussed.
We recognise that having a child with additional needs can be challenging. We aim to support you and your child and strive to work together to achieve the best possible outcome for every child at our school.
Should your child attend this school and you feel dissatisfied with any element of our SEND provision, initially speak to the class teacher. If you feel the issue has not been resolved please arrange a meeting with the SENDCo or the Head Teacher. If you continue to feel dissatisfied, the school has a SEND Governor who can advise you. Her name is Lisa Worley; please contact the schools office to gain contact details or arrange a meeting.
For further information please visit our Trust website. A key document is the SEND policy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wagtail Class – Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page
pageCache.text:
Mrs Baker & Mrs Stancombe
Wagtail Class is a magical place where children start their primary journey with us. A classroom full of wonder, led by a curiosity from each individual child – it’s a delightful place to start their primary adventure.
This class is well supported by experienced and amazing TAs, Mrs Goddard and Mrs Blakey. With small class sizes, our Reception children get a really fantastic journey through the foundation stage, getting a strong start to their education and being able to learn from the Y1 children who they share the class with.

pageCache.pageTitle: Skylark Class – Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page
pageCache.text:
Mrs Mitchell-Mallon
Skylark Class is a combination of our Y2, Y3 and some Y4 children, and is where they continue their National Curriculum journey. They get off to a fantastic start with curious questions being posed, excellent teaching and a positive atmosphere. The Key Stage 1 journey is a special and critical one and it is great to see the learning that these children do each day as they complete their KS1 programme of study and begin their adventure in to Key Stage 2, with a curriculum based on answering key questions in each subject.
The teaching of English and maths is split in Skylark class so the Y2 children receive they key learning they require, whilst the Y3 and Y4 children come together for their KS2 learning. The class is well supported by experienced and fantastic TAs, Mrs Booth and Miss MacDougall.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our School Council – Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page
pageCache.text:
Our School Council
Established in January 2023, the school council is a group of students and teachers who work together to create a positive and inclusive school community.
We strive to make our school a place where every student can feel valued and supported, and where their unique talents and abilities can be celebrated. Our vision is to “let your light shine,” drawing inspiration from Matthew 5:16, which reminds us that we are all called to be a shining example of respect, kindness, and resilience.
As members of the school council, they work to make this vision a reality by fostering a culture of our vision, and by providing opportunities for students to get involved and make a difference in our school and beyond.
As well as looking to develop and improve opportunities for their own school, our council also look at how they can help others shine their lights brightly, through charitable work and raising awareness.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing and Mental Health – Stone with Woodford C. of E. Primary School – Home page
pageCache.text:
As a school, we take wellbeing very seriously and are keen for all children and staff to be able to access the support they need and focus on their mental health. We have weekly mindfulness sessions in school, with our mindfulness coach, Cathy Blofeld.
Please find below a range of resources and websites that we have come across that may be helpful in supporting the mental wellbeing of both your child and your whole family.
We also know that talking to someone who is ready to listen can be the best kind of support so please do contact us with any concerns about a child’s, or your own, mental wellbeing. We are always here to listen and to give advice or support.
If you are part of any organisation or you have any experience that you feel may help us to support the wellbeing of the children and staff then do let us know.
